chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'ir from Harun ibn Hamzah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When the time for a prescribed prayer enters, begin with it before performing the prayer over the deceased, unless the deceased is a postpartum woman or similar."
ai.seo_question: Which takes precedence: the prescribed prayer or the funeral prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the hierarchy between the fixed-time obligatory prayer (Salat al-Maktubah) and the funeral prayer (Salat al-Janazah), establishing that the former takes precedence unless the deceased is in a state of major impurity (Janabah) or a postpartum woman (Nufas), where the funeral prayer may be performed first to avoid delay. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on not delaying the Fard prayer beyond its prescribed time, even for the honor of the deceased. The exception highlights the practical consideration of the deceased's ritual state, ensuring the funeral prayer is not unnecessarily postponed if the body is already prepared for burial.
